hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement depends on the σ-algebra on `U`. The only measure is `μHE[finrank ℝ U]`, which is `Measure V` (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure` in Mathlib's `Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean` uses only the metric, `MeasurableSpace V` and `BorelSpace V`). The rest of the statement (tsums over subsets of `U`, `DifferentiableAt`, `fderiv`, `normDet`) does not mention `MeasurableSpace U` at all. The proof uses `[MeasurableSpace U] [BorelSpace U]` only through `LipschitzWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_compl_setOf_regular` (Lipschitz.lean:175). That lemma needs them for Rademacher's theorem and volume on `U`, but its conclusion `μHE[finrank ℝ U] (f '' {x | …}ᶜ) = 0` also does not involve the measurable structure of `U`. So without `[BorelSpace U]` (keeping the arbitrary `[MeasurableSpace U]`, which the statement then ignores), the proof becomes: `letI : MeasurableSpace U := borel U; haveI : BorelSpace U := ⟨rfl⟩`, then the same `filter_upwards [measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem.mp hf.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_compl_setOf_regular]` and the rest of the proof as is. The lemma's conclusion is literally the same proposition whichever `MeasurableSpace U` instance is used. No degenerate cases arise, because the change is only about which σ-algebra on `U` is used inside the proof. `[MeasurableSpace U]` cannot be deleted on its own, because the type of `[BorelSpace U]` mentions it. It is only extra together with `BorelSpace U`, so only `[BorelSpace U]` is reported.
